overview: Azerbaijan is a country in the South Caucasus, on the western shore of the Caspian Sea. Its capital and largest city is Baku. Azerbaijan became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991. Oil and gas are the backbone of its economy, and the area around Baku was one of the world's first major oil-producing regions.

geography.text: The Greater Caucasus mountains run along Azerbaijan's northern border, and the Lesser Caucasus rise in the west. Between them lies a wide lowland crossed by the Kura river. Parts of the coast are below sea level, because the Caspian Sea itself is below sea level. The region of Nakhchivan is separated from the rest of the country by Armenia.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Ranges from dry semi-desert near Baku to wet subtropical forests in the south.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Gazelles live on the dry plains, and sturgeon swim in the Caspian Sea.

history.text: The region was ruled by Persian empires and shaped by Turkic peoples who arrived from the 1000s. Russia took control in the early 1800s. Azerbaijan declared independence in 1918 as one of the first democratic republics in the Muslim world, before being absorbed into the Soviet Union. It became independent again in 1991 and has fought wars with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Persia gives up the region to Russia.

events.title: First republic
events.text: The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic is declared.

events.title: Soviet takeover
events.text: The Red Army ends the republic.

events.title: Karabakh retaken
events.text: Azerbaijan takes full control of Nagorno-Karabakh.

government.text: Azerbaijan is a presidential republic in which power is concentrated in the President. Ilham Aliyev has held the office since 2003, after his father Heydar Aliyev. Term limits were removed in 2009. International observers have criticised its elections and treatment of journalists.

economy.text: Oil and natural gas from the Caspian Sea make up most of Azerbaijan's exports. Pipelines carry them to Türkiye and Europe. The government is trying to grow other industries such as farming and tourism.

culture.text: Azerbaijan mixes Turkic, Persian and Russian influences. Its music, mugham, is listed by UNESCO, as are its carpets. Baku's Old City, with the Maiden Tower, is a UNESCO site, and the country is called the 'Land of Fire' because of natural gas fires that burn on its hillsides.

items.title: Yanar Dag
items.text: A hillside where natural gas has burned for decades.

items.title: Mugham
items.text: Improvised classical music, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Flame Towers
items.text: Three skyscrapers in Baku lit up like flames.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Plov, rice with saffron and meat, and dolma.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Mugham music and hand-woven carpets are listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Novruz, the spring festival, involves jumping over bonfires and growing green wheat sprouts called semeni.

sport.text: Wrestling, judo and chess are Azerbaijan's strongest sports. Baku hosted the first European Games in 2015 and has held a Formula 1 Grand Prix through its streets since 2016.

items.text: Baku hosted the first European Games.

didYouKnow: Azerbaijan has about half of all the world's mud volcanoes.
One of the world's first oil wells was drilled near Baku in 1846.

keyPeople.name: Nizami Ganjavi
keyPeople.text: A great Persian-language poet of the 1100s.

keyPeople.name: Lotfi Zadeh
keyPeople.text: Grew up in Baku and invented fuzzy logic.
